ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the centroid of $\triangle ABC$ is $G$, and point $D$ is on the extension line of $CB$, with $BD = \frac{1}{2}BC$. The line passing through points $D$ and $G$ intersects $AC$ at point $E$. What is the value of $\frac{AE}{AC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, extend CG and intersect AB at F, extend AG and intersect BC at H, connect FH which intersects DE at N,\\
$\because$ G is the centroid of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $FH$ is the midline of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $FH\parallel AC$,\\
$\because$ $BD=\frac{1}{2}BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $BD=BH=CH$,\\
$\because$ $NH\parallel EC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DH}{DC}=\frac{NH}{EC}=\frac{2}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $EC=\frac{3}{2}NH$,\\
$\because$ $NH\parallel AE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{NH}{EA}=\frac{HG}{AG}=\frac{1}{2}$, thus $AE=2NH$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{CE}=\frac{2NH}{\frac{3}{2}NH}=\frac{4}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{AC}=\boxed{\frac{4}{7}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B and C are below on the same straight line; point D is located on the extension of CB and is on the left side of B, so D, B, C are collinear. Point G is inside the triangle, and line DG intersects side AC at point E. Reasoning: Use the affine coordinate method, because affine transformations preserve collinearity relations and length ratios on the same straight line. Let B=(0,0), C=(2,0); from BD=1/2 BC, get D=(-1,0). Take a convenient non-collinear point A=(0,1). Since G is the centroid of triangle ABC, G=((0+0+2)/3,(1+0+0)/3)=(2/3,1/3). Suppose E is on AC, written as E=A+t(C-A)=(2t,1-t), where t=AE/AC. On the other hand, E is also on line DG, whose parametric form is D+s(G-D)=(-1,0)+s((2/3,1/3)-(-1,0))=(-1+5s/3,s/3). Set the two representations equal, obtaining 2t=-1+5s/3, 1-t=s/3. From 1-t=s/3 get s=3(1-t), substitute into the first equation: 2t=-1+5(1-t)=4-5t, so 7t=4, t=4/7. Therefore AE/AC=4/7.
